Amos was a shepherd whom God called to prophesy. How does God use ordinary people?
God judged nations for cruelty. What does this show about God's concern for how people are treated?
Judah rejected the law of the Lord. What happens when God's people neglect his word?
Israel sold the needy for a pair of sandals. How might we overlook the poor today?
"You only have I known... therefore I will punish you." What responsibility comes with knowing God?
"The Lord God does nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets." How does God speak to his people?
God sent hardships, but "yet you did not return to me." How does God use hardship to call us back?
"Prepare to meet your God, O Israel!" How do you prepare to meet God?
"Seek me and live." What does seeking God look like for you?
"Seek good, and not evil, that you may live... Hate evil, and love good, and establish justice." How can you do this?
"Let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream." What does God want more than religious show?
"Woe to those who are at ease in Zion." How can comfort make us careless?
They lay on beds of ivory but did not grieve over the ruin of Joseph. What suffering might you be ignoring?
Amos prayed, "O Lord God, please forgive!" and God relented. What does this show about prayer?
Amos said, "I was no prophet... the Lord took me from following the flock." How has God called you from ordinary life?
Some cheated the poor with dishonest scales. How can you be honest in your dealings?
God warned of a famine of hearing the words of the Lord. How much do you value God's word?
God will raise up the fallen booth of David. How does Acts 15 see this fulfilled?
"I will restore the fortunes of my people." What does this hope mean to you?
